subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit + prompt collection for Acme Corp - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-17T16:35:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + action items (Model fit / prompt collection)

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Goal: Validate model fit for Acme’s customer support summarization and account-redaction workflow (high throughput, <300ms token latency target for 99th percentile).
2) Suggested models to benchmark (starting points): redwood-3b-8k (default), redwood-7b-8k-quant (cost-optimized with quant), and a conservative open baseline (gpt-j-6B) for head-to-head quality comparisons.
3) What we need from you: a representative prompt set (50-200 prompts) that includes: common cases, failure/edge cases, example outputs you expect, and any fields that must be redacted or tokenized (PII / account numbers).
4) Deliverables from Redwood: a short benchmark report (latency / token cost / ROUGE/BLEU-style quality checks) and a shortlist of recommended model/config+quant settings.

Attachments: I’m attaching a prompt_set_template.csv to make submission easier. Also linking our internal benchmark folder here: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/benchmark-acme-2026

Request: Can you send the prompt set and any redaction rules by EOD Thursday 3/19? If that’s tight, even a first batch of 30 prompts will let us do an initial fit test.

One note on privacy: please remove direct customer emails and swap account numbers with consistent tokens (we can provide redaction guidance below). Priyom (cc) will follow up with a one-page redaction guide.

Next steps:
- You: upload prompts + redaction notes -> drive link or reply with attached CSV
- Us: run model fit bench and share recommended model + config by 3/24

Thanks — excited to get this running.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Li <rachel.li@acme.com>
Date: 2026-03-17T18:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + action items (Model fit / prompt collection)

Thanks Marissa — clear plan, appreciate the template. A few clarifications from our side: 

- PII: We can remove customer emails and replace with <EMAIL_REDACTED>. For account IDs we have patterns like ACME-ORD-123456 and also legacy numeric-only IDs (e.g., 987654321). For the latter, would you prefer masking last 3 digits or full tokenization?
- Edge cases: we’ll include prompts that intentionally contain multi-issue tickets, non-English snippets, and corrupted UTF-8 characters (we’ve seen them).
- Output expectations: Ideally we get a structured JSON with fields {summary, top_issue, recommended_action, confidence}. Do you have a recommended schema?

I attached a quick dump of 12 real prompts (scrubbed) to start (initial_prompts.txt). We can escalate to CSV once you confirm the redaction pattern.

Sam
Sam Jenkins
Senior Support Ops Manager | Acme Corp
sam.jenkins@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-17T19:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + action items (Model fit / prompt collection)

Sam — great, thanks for the quick reply and the sample file. Short answers:

- Account IDs: please replace any IDs with a consistent token like <ACCOUNT_ID_x> where x is a small integer per unique account in the set (e.g., <ACCOUNT_ID_1>, <ACCOUNT_ID_2>). For high-risk IDs (full SSN-like numbers) please fully redact to <REDACTED_PII>. If you prefer deterministic masking, masking the last 3 digits is also fine (e.g., 987654***).
- Output schema: Yes — the structured schema you suggested is perfect for evaluation. We’ll validate against: summary (string), top_issue (string), recommended_action (string), confidence (0-1 float). If you can include an example expected output for 10 of the prompts that’s very helpful for quality checks.

I’ve dropped the template CSV in the thread (prompt_set_template.csv). Priyom will attach a one-pager redaction guide (redaction_guidance.pdf) and a sample expected-outputs.csv to show the example annotations.

Model guidance: start with redwood-3b-8k for throughput checks. If quality looks marginal on summaries we’ll run redwood-7b-8k-quant and compare. For cost-sensitive long-tail tickets we can try the quantized variants.

Thanks — we’ll wait for the CSV. If you can get 50 prompts it will give a more stable quality signal, but the 12 you sent are sufficient for a first pass.

Best,
Marissa

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-03-18T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: redaction guidance + prompt template (attached)

Hi Sam —

Attaching the redaction one-pager and a prompt_set_template.csv (columns: id, prompt_text, context_meta, expected_output_json, tags). A few quick tips from the SE side: 

- Keep prompts as close to production wording as possible; include the ticket text and any metadata fields (subject, product, priority).
- For multi-issue tickets include a separate prompt row for each expected summary/action to help the eval metric.
- For confidence annotation use a 0-1 float; if unsure, leave blank and we’ll compute model confidence distribution.

Attachment stubs: prompt_set_template.csv (CSV template), redaction_guidance.pdf (one-page).

If helpful I can jump on a 15-min call with your team tomorrow to walk through the template.

Priyom
